summary.short: Anatel Resolution 777/2025 approves the General Telecommunications Services Regulation (RGST), revoking or replacing numerous earlier Anatel rules. Binding on telecom service providers: licensing, interconnection, number portability, emergency services, fraud prevention, subscriber data and consumer duties. Article 40 sets principles for providers' AI-based solutions. Generally in force 180 days after publication.
summary.long: Anatel Resolution 777/2025 approves the General Telecommunications Services Regulation (RGST), annexed to it, and revokes, replaces or amends numerous earlier Anatel regulations (Arts. 1-26). The Annex sets rules for public and private telecom services, authorization and licensing, equipment certification and networks. Article 40 requires providers using AI-based solutions to observe listed principles, including reliability, non-discrimination, privacy and transparency and explainability. Other provisions cover interconnection, number portability through a central database and an administering entity, provider and user duties, record retention for set periods, free access to emergency services, secrecy and data retention limits, fraud prevention, maximum charges for certain shared-rate calls, and mandatory distribution of certain TV channels. Sanctions are referred to other regulation (Art. 40 sole paragraph; Art. 43 §6); no penalty amounts appear in this text. Most provisions apply from 180 days after publication (Art. 28), and the header notes that some deadlines were postponed by Anatel orders. The document provided covers the instrument through Title V, Chapter II of the Annex.
